PASS: PASS (round 1). Audited commit b13ee9a, working tree clean, sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. All 9 requirements met. This one I did not audit by reading alone - I compiled the real route handler, stubbed only lib/items and lib/format so every dispatch decision stayed the handlers own, and drove it. Findings below are observed behaviour, not inference.

REQUIREMENTS COVERAGE - all MET:
Req 1: a real DELETE FROM items WHERE claim_token = $1. Not an UPDATE, not a flag. Grepped the whole app tree for deleted_at, is_deleted, soft-delete, audit and archive: nothing. No migration in this commit, so no soft-delete column was added. Deliberately no RETURNING clause, which means the deleted row data is never in scope in that function at all - there is nothing there that could reach a log line even by accident. That is containment by construction rather than by remembering, the same instinct as sprint 3 CreatedItem.
Req 1, success determination: deleteItemByToken returns (result.rowCount ?? 0) > 0 - the drivers own reported count of rows affected, never the absence of an exception. The ?? 0 guards a null rowCount rather than letting it coerce. This is the specific thing the sprints top risk is about and it is done right.
Req 1/4: the write is authorized by the token on the write itself - the DELETE is keyed on claim_token, not on anything the rendering step established. Not wired to GET: the GET handler never references deleteItemByToken at all.
Req 2: remove control renders on the claim page alongside the claim control, as two independent forms. The board itself gains no removal control.
Req 3: DEMONSTRATED, this being the destructive one. I drove the real POST handler with six different action values and watched which database function each request actually reached. action=remove reaches findItemByClaimToken only and returns the 200 interstitial - no delete. action=remove-confirmed is the only value in the entire file that reaches deleteItemByToken. The rendered item page only ever emits remove, so a single click cannot destroy a row; the second, distinct click on the interstitials own form is what deletes. This is a server-side dispatch requirement, not a client-side confirm() in front of an unguarded endpoint - the criterion names that failure mode explicitly and this is not it.
Req 3, stated plainly so it is on the record: the two steps are stateless - the server does not track that step 1 occurred, so a caller can post remove-confirmed directly. That is not a gap. The requirement names an interstitial as an acceptable form, the threat it addresses is an accidental misclick rather than a determined caller, and anyone able to post that value already holds the token, which by this products design is full authority over the row. Nothing is reachable here that the token does not already grant.
Req 4: DEMONSTRATED. A GET through the real handler reaches findItemByClaimToken only, never deleteItemByToken. There is no branch under GET that reaches removal, so a link previewer, crawler or HEAD request cannot destroy a post.
Req 5: DEMONSTRATED byte-for-byte, not by inspection. I compared the response for a removed item against the response for a token that never existed: both 404, bodies byte-identical under Buffer.compare, no removed or deleted wording anywhere in the body, and no token in it. They are identical because they are literally the same function returning the same frozen literal - notFoundResponse() - not two branches that happen to match today. After a successful delete the handler redirects to the same GET URL, which finds no row and takes the ordinary not-found branch, so there is no special-case removed path that could drift.
Req 6: DEMONSTRATED. Rendered the item page with claimed false and claimed true: the remove form is present in both. The claim form correctly disappears once claimed, the remove form does not.
Req 7: falls out of the existing force-dynamic board read - the row is gone, so it cannot be listed.
Req 8: traced and confirmed. The delete is wrapped, a thrown error returns errorResponse() and that branch is checked before the not-deleted branch can run, so a database failure cannot reach the success redirect and cannot fall through to not-found. A user whose delete did not commit is told it failed, not that it worked and not that their post never existed. Both failure bodies are generic; no connection string, host, credential or driver detail reaches any response. Detail goes to console.error only, and every console call in this file takes the caught error, never an item.
Req 9: docs/runbook-remove-item.md exists and is genuinely usable - a row-identification SELECT, the DELETE keyed on id, and a confirming SELECT that expects zero rows. The irreversibility warning is present and explicit. Keying the operator path on id rather than claim_token is the right call and is explained: a moderator should not need the posters own secret to act.

SPRINT 3 GUARANTEES STILL INTACT, checked rather than assumed: claim_token appears in no SELECT or RETURNING list anywhere - only in the INSERT column list, two WHERE clauses and the DELETE WHERE clause. Neither rendered page contains the token, verified by searching both rendered bodies for a known token value: zero occurrences on the item page and zero on the new confirmation interstitial. Both new forms omit the action attribute, so sprint 3 round 1 fix was not quietly undone by the file being rewritten around it. next.config.ts is untouched, so noindex and no-referrer still apply to /claim/:token.

NEW XSS SURFACE CHECKED: the confirmation interstitial interpolates the item title into its prose. Ran a script-tag title through the real render path - comes back entity-escaped, not executable.

FILE OWNERSHIP RESPECTED: the commit touches lib/items.ts, app/claim/** and the runbook only. It does not touch app/api/items/route.ts or app/page.tsx, which the sprint file assigns to sprint 5. Verified against the commits own file list, not against the handoff claim. Sprint 5 is on its own branch in a separate worktree, so the parallel boundary held in both directions.

ALSO: npm run lint exit 0, npm run build exit 0, both run by me.

NON-BLOCKING, not holding this gate:
1. Dispatch is fail-open on unrecognised input, demonstrated: any action value the handler does not recognise - delete, a case variant like REMOVE-CONFIRMED, or a missing/malformed form body - falls through to the default branch and CLAIMS the item. Nothing destructive, idempotent, requires the token, and it preserves sprint 3 behaviour for a bare POST, so it is not a requirement violation. But an unrecognised input performing a mutation is the wrong default in principle; an explicit action === claim check with a 400 otherwise would be tighter. Worth noting that the fail-open direction is at least the safe one - a mistyped remove-confirmed claims rather than deletes.
2. Carried from sprint 3, still unaddressed and still out of scope: the absolute Location built from request.url where a relative one would be proxy-immune, and app/layout.tsx default Create Next App metadata title. The stale lib/format.ts comment referencing components/claim-form.tsx also remains.

CLEARED for /sprint-dev-done then Pipeman. LiveQA owns what static analysis cannot settle, and two of its criteria matter more than usual here: confirming via direct read-only SQL that the row is actually absent rather than hidden, which is the only check that can tell a hard delete from a filtered soft one, and forcing a real database failure against the removal path. Dev Team has a fresh poisoned preview standing that they report reflects this sprints code - LiveQA should confirm that for itself rather than taking it on the handoff, since sprint 3 preview turned out to predate the fix under test.

PASS: PASS - live test round 1. All nine requirements verified live against commit 9b7e418, including Req 8's forced database failure on the destructive path.

Env: Reqs 1-7 and 9 on production deployment mdk2rzmei (githubCommitSha 07a453e, app code identical to shipped 9b7e418 - git diff shows only docs/sprints/state/sprint-4.json). Req 8 on preview deployment c2nzpm71f. Tested 2026-09-21 22:33-22:38 UTC with curl and read-only SQL against Neon.

PREVIEW PROVENANCE - INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED, WHICH IS WHAT QA1 AND PIPEMAN ASKED FOR.
Both flagged that the Dev-Team-provided preview needed verification rather than trust-on-handoff, given sprint 3 burned a round on a stale one. I did not evaluate anyone's reasoning; I pulled the deployment metadata from Vercel's API directly:
  c2nzpm71f: target=preview, readyState=READY, source=cli, githubCommitSha=b13ee9ae85dbadee91cdbb25bd9a989686fb2ec3, message "Sprint 4: poster-initiated post removal (Reqs 1-9)".
  b13ee9a is the commit QA1 audited and PASSed. git diff b13ee9a..9b7e418 over app/, lib/, package.json, next.config.ts, tsconfig.json and the runbook is EMPTY - the only difference between the preview's commit and the shipped commit is docs/sprints/state/sprint-4.json. So this preview carries the shipped application code.
  I also confirmed it is genuinely poisoned before trusting it as a failure environment: /api/health returns 503 "Service unavailable" there, while production's /api/health returns 200 "ok".
  THIS ONE IS VALID. That is a different answer from sprint 3, and the contrast is worth recording: sprint 3's preview quy71v4l8 carries githubCommitSha db295c1, which was the commit QA1 CONDITIONALed, superseded by the fix 4fc6843. The same metadata check that cleared this preview is what condemned that one. The check is cheap and it has now produced both answers, which is the argument for running it every time rather than reasoning about whether a fix "touched error handling".

ON "WHO DEPLOYED IT", WHICH I CANNOT SETTLE AND SHOULD NOT PRETEND TO. Pipeman asked that provenance include who stood the preview up, not just what commit it carries. Vercel's metadata reports creator=samuelaraki and source=cli for this preview - and for every other deployment in this project, including Pipeman's own and the one I created myself in sprint 3, because they all authenticate with the same account token. The platform cannot distinguish which role's session issued a deploy. So I can answer "what code is in it" conclusively and I cannot answer "which session made it" at all. Pipeman's process concern - that a Dev Team session standing up its own deployments creates a second, invisible way for a stale preview to be trusted - stands entirely on its own merits and is not something my gate can verify either way. Worth raising with Dev Team directly, as Pipeman suggested; my verdict rests on the commit, not on the chain of custody.

Req 1 - hard delete, verified by direct SQL, which is the only check that can tell a hard delete from a filtered soft delete: PASS.
  After removing item 19 (unclaimed) and item 20 (claimed first), a direct query returns rows matching those ids: 0.
  The items table columns are unchanged from sprint 2: id, title, price_cents, email, claimed, claim_token, created_at. There is no deleted_at, no is_deleted, no soft-delete flag of any kind.
  Tables in the public schema: items, and nothing else. There is no audit or archive table retaining the removed email addresses.

Req 2 - removal control on the claim page: PASS. The page renders both "Mark as claimed" and "Remove this post", as two separate <form method="POST"> elements carrying hidden inputs action=claim and action=remove. The board itself still exposes no removal control.

Req 3 - explicit confirmation before execution: PASS, and tested the way the requirement actually specifies - by attempting the removal WITHOUT confirming.
  POST action=remove returned HTTP 200 and rendered an interstitial: "Confirm removal. Remove \"LiveQA S4 Remove Unclaimed\" from the board? This permanently deletes the post and cannot be undone." with a single button "Yes, permanently remove this post" and a hidden input action=remove-confirmed.
  The item was NOT deleted by that request - board ids after it were [21, 20, 19], with 19 still present. A single click cannot destroy the row.
  This is a server-rendered interstitial, not a client-side confirm() in front of an unguarded endpoint: the destructive action requires a different action value than the one the visible button sends, and the unconfirmed value provably does not delete.

Req 4 - not reachable by GET: PASS, tested well beyond a browser GET.
  Against item 21: GET 200, HEAD 200, Slackbot-LinkExpanding 200, Twitterbot 200, facebookexternalhit 200, WhatsApp 200, and GET /claim/<token>?action=remove 200. DELETE returns 405.
  After all seven, item 21 was still present on the board. A link previewer, crawler or prefetch cannot destroy a post.

Req 5 - removed link is byte-identical to any invalid token: PASS, compared byte-for-byte rather than judged by eye.
  Four responses: removed-unclaimed token, removed-after-claim token, a made-up a*64 token, and a malformed "zzz-not-a-token". All four returned HTTP 404 at 170 bytes with the SAME sha256 (f534490b0c01bf0fc033057aaf8ef63b...). cmp confirms all three comparisons against the made-up token are IDENTICAL.
  Body-revealing headers also match across all four: same status, same content-type, same x-robots-tag: noindex, same referrer-policy: no-referrer.
  POST to a removed token and POST to a made-up token likewise produced identical bodies and identical 404s - deletion does not leak that a token was once valid, on either method.
  Corroborating the "same code path" requirement rather than mere coincidence: this sha256 f534490b... is the identical hash I recorded for sprint 3's not-found response. The removed-item response is not a new branch that happens to match today; it is the same response sprint 3 shipped.

Req 6 - works on claimed and unclaimed items: PASS. Item 19 was removed while unclaimed. Item 20 was claimed first (confirmed claimed=true via the API) and then removed through the same two-step flow. Both rows are gone from the database.

Req 7 - removed item gone for a cold client: PASS. A client with a fresh cookie jar and a distinct User-Agent, which had never loaded the page, saw only the one remaining item. The removed titles appear 0 times and - the point of the whole sprint - the removed email addresses rm-unclaimed@example.com and rm-claimed@example.com each appear 0 times in the page. cache-control: private, no-cache, no-store and x-vercel-cache: MISS, so no redeploy was involved.

Req 8 - database failure surfaces as an error, never as success and never as not-found: PASS.
  I MIS-BUILT THIS COMPARISON, THE SAME WAY I MIS-BUILT SPRINT 3'S, AND AM RECORDING IT BECAUSE ONCE IS A SLIP AND TWICE IS A PATTERN. My first pass compared the confirmed-removal response against a made-up token ON THE POISONED PREVIEW, found them byte-identical, and my own output labelled that "IDENTICAL to not-found = FAIL". It is not. On a preview with a dead database BOTH requests are database errors, so of course they match, and matching is correct. The genuine not-found only exists where the database is healthy. I caught the identical mistake in sprint 3 and still constructed the check the same wrong way here, so the specific lesson worth carrying is: the not-found half of this comparison must always be fetched from a HEALTHY deployment, never from the poisoned one.
  The correct comparison:
    Case A - confirmed removal, DB DOWN:      HTTP 503, "Error Could not load this claim link right now. Please try again later."  (sha 42cc9659...)
    Case B - genuine not-found, DB HEALTHY:   HTTP 404, "Claim link not found This claim link is not valid."                        (sha f534490b...)
  Different status, different text, different hash. A poster trying to get their email off a public page during an outage is told to try again later; they are never told the post is already gone.
  The three outcomes Req 8 forbids or requires, evaluated on the confirmed-removal response under a dead database:
    claims SUCCESS (removed/deleted/has been)? -> False
    claims NOT FOUND?                          -> False
    surfaces an ERROR?                         -> True
  All three steps of the flow fail safe: GET the claim page, POST action=remove, and POST action=remove-confirmed each return 503 with the same error text.
  CONSISTENCY, 5 consecutive confirmed-removal attempts under the dead database: HTTP 503 and the identical message every time, never flipping to success or to not-found.
  MOST IMPORTANT: THE ROW SURVIVED. After 6 failed removal attempts against the poisoned deployment, a direct SQL query against the real database still returns item 21 with its email intact. The failure did not partially commit, and the user was not told otherwise. This is the exact scenario the sprint file names as its worst outcome - a user believing their email is off a public board when it is not - and it does not occur.
  LEAK SWEEP over body and headers, 15 patterns (postgres, neon, password, notarealpassword, 127.0.0.1, ECONNREFUSED, ENOTFOUND, :5432, DATABASE_URL, stack-frame "at fn (", /var/task, /vercel/, node_modules, pg-pool, sslmode): ZERO hits. The token is echoed back into the failure body 0 times.

Req 9 - committed runbook: PASS as observed (QA1 owns this statically). docs/runbook-remove-item.md exists at 1962 bytes, contains runnable SQL - "DELETE FROM items WHERE id = 123;" and a verification "SELECT id FROM items WHERE id = 123;" - and carries the irreversibility warning: "**This is irreversible.** `DELETE` here is a real, permanent removal".

SPRINT 3'S GUARANTEES STILL INTACT on this commit: the claim route still sends x-robots-tag: noindex and referrer-policy: no-referrer, on success responses, on 404s, and on database-failure responses alike.

PARALLEL-WORK BOUNDARY RESPECTED: commit b13ee9a touches exactly three files - app/claim/[token]/route.ts, lib/items.ts, and docs/runbook-remove-item.md. It does not touch app/api/items/route.ts or app/page.tsx, which the sprint file assigns to sprint 5. Noting it because two sprints are in flight; sprint 5 sits in a separate worktree at dev_build and the status command flagged the divergence, which is expected parallel work rather than a problem.

PRODUCTION WAS NOT TOUCHED by the Req 8 testing: all forced-failure requests went to the preview, production's own /api/health returned 200 throughout, and no stored environment variable was modified.

HOUSEKEEPING: test data cleanup is handled separately, per the standing preference established in sprint 2. Leftover forced-failure previews now number five across the project (292jy7q6n, ppnbpzjon, quy71v4l8, rng0kfb29, c2nzpm71f); all are preview targets carrying noindex and none ever touched production.

VERDICT PASS = THE CODE IS READY, NOT THAT ANYONE MAY CLOSE THIS. /sprint-complete requires the user's explicit real-time authorization via --user-said. Both gates being green is not authorization. Dev Team tells the user it is ready and waits.
